text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Central Bank denies reports that several companies in Kuwait were being used to launder money.
- Kuwait lays to rest Sheikh Ali Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah. The senior member of the ruling family and former minister of defence died in London on Sunday.
- Government offices close for five days starting April 16 to mark Moslem Eid al-Adha feast.
- Sheep prices rise ahead of Moslem feast.

- Kuwait's Prime Minister and Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah left for the United States from Britain for further medical tests. He flew to London on March 10 after a colon surgery in Kuwait.
- Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah heads mourners at Sheikh Ali's funeral.
- Central Bank warns against fictitious business deals with foreign parties.
- Interior Ministry urges Kuwaitis to hand in arms abandoned by a fleeing Iraqi army at the end of the 1991 Gulf War.
- Some 30 fuel stations to be privatised within weeks as a first step.
